learning_objective: 🎯 Meet the action heroes of grammar and their trusty sidekicks to build powerful sentences!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Main verbs are the superstar action words in a sentence! They tell us exactly what someone is doing, like jump, read, eat, sleep, or sing.
Auxiliary means 'helper'! These verbs help the main verb to show time or make questions. Common helpers are is, am, are, was, were, has, and have.
In the sentence 'She IS PLAYING football', 'is' is the helpful auxiliary verb, and 'playing' is the main action verb. They work together perfectly!

fun_activity.title: ✏️ The Helper Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Write down this sentence: 'I am reading a great book.' Circle the helper verb (am) with a red crayon and underline the main verb (reading) with a blue crayon!

quick_recap: ⭐ Main verbs show the real action happening in the sentence.
⭐ Auxiliary verbs are helping words like is, am, are, was, and were.
⭐ Helping verbs and main verbs often hold hands to work together in a sentence!
